item.title: From a Rio Favela to City Hall: How Education Changed Everything for Me
item.description: At 27, Salvino Oliveira went from being a street vendor in Rio's Cidade de Deus to a city councilor leading education reform. This followed him starting his first social project: making tuition free for poor children at 15 years old. In recognition of his efforts towards making education more accessible, Oliveira has been honored as a 2025 Young Activist Summit Laureate. In 2018, he became an activist, and as civic space in Brazil is obstructed, he was warned of the dangers. Still, he persisted.

item.description: Dieu-Nalio Chery is a Michigan-based, Haitian-born photographer working as a staff photographer at the University of Michigan and a freelance photojournalist across The New York Times, Reuters, Washington Post, Haitian Times, and The Associated Press. item.title: The Malaria Vaccine Deal That Could Save Millions — Here’s What to Know
item.description: For decades, the world made steady progress toward one of the most ambitious targets set by the UN’s Global Goals: ensuring that no child dies from a preventable disease by 2030. item.title: Why Is a 100-Year-Old Vaccine Still Our Only Defense Against the World’s Deadliest Infectious Disease?
item.description: Tuberculosis (TB), the world’s oldest infectious disease, is also one of its deadliest. In 2024 alone, TB killed about 1.23 million people — more than the combined tolls from malaria and HIV/AIDS combined. item.title: Two Drops and a Long Walk: Inside Mozambique’s Door-to-Door Polio Vaccination Drive
item.description: Polio vaccination workers don't just deliver two lifesaving drops — sometimes they even name a child.
